newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Montreal to buy back 3 pct of shrs.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Montreal to buy back 3 pct of shrs.

text.p: Bank of Montreal said on Wednesday it plans to buy back for cancellation up to 7.5 million of its common shares, or about three percent of its outstanding stock, during the year.
The bank also said it has publicly issued C$400 million of non-cumulative preferred shares in the domestic market.

BMO has issued 16 million non-cumulative class B preferred shares, series 3, priced at C$25 per share to yield 5.55 percent. The shares will be redeemable by the bank at a declining premium after August 2004 for cash or for common shares at 95 percent of the market price of the common shares.

They will also be convertible by the holder into Bank of Montreal common shares after May 2007 at 95 percent of the prevailing market price, subject to BMO's pre-emptive right to redeem the shares for cash or find substitute purchasers.
The bank said the 1997 share purchase program follows purchase programs of 3.5 million shares in 1995 and 5.0 million shares in 1996.
The share purchase programs, established in 1995, were designed as an additional means for ensuring that the bank maintains an optimal level of capital to support the growth of its business.

The repurchase program was approved by the bank's board and the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, and will be carried out as a normal course issuer bid on the Toronto and Montreal stock exchanges.
BMO will proceed with the program once all remaining regulatory approvals have been obtained.
